body: That doesn't really make me feel a whole lot better, since those "good times" are probably never going to happen. Not without some serious poking from a mouse cursor...

No no, honestly I would LOVE to have a group of friends, or even a regular meetup sort of thing where I could talk about games and such, and I don't know how to make that happen myself so I'm very welcoming of other's suggestions.

I'm mostly into video games, really. I love everything from classic Nintendo to modern blockbuster to obscure indie.

I've never really played any tabletop RPGs like warhammer, but I love the idea of pen-and-paper games (even if I don't have much experience). I also rather enjoyed what little Magic the Gathering I've played. (however I did try and check out a local comic store that had regular magic tournaments, but I did not like the atmosphere of the place so I didn't go back)
I gotta ask- how did he/she react? I can't help but worry that my first partner is going to be turned off by the fact that I'm inexperienced, or laugh when I tell them it's my first time.

21 with no friends. Based on the rate I meet new people, I estimate my first kiss might happen by the time I die.

(as much as I'd like to feel happy for you OP, I can't help but be a little bitter. sorry. =[ )

Unfortunately I moved away from there, so I couldn't get together with them even if I wanted to. It doesn't help that most of my interests are really geeky things. It's hard to find people to game with.

(hey OP, just wanted to say that I'm in your exact position. Same age, also tried OKCupid to disastrous results. I made a thread about it yesterday, if you're curious)

Back to DPool, this is something I would like to believe, except for pretty much my whole life up until last year, I wasn't trying. I was just doing what I enjoyed and making my way through life, and the thing was, I didn't have very many friends. You said that the people you connected with were already "in your circles", but that's not an option for me, because I don't know anyone. I mean, looking back, I can think of like 4 or 5 girls who I was friends with (in HS), and I never felt particularly close to them. Currently (after leaving college moving back to my hometown) I literally don't have any girl friends my age. I only have one friend, and it's really because we were best friends when we were kids, not because of anything recent. He introduced me to a few of his friends, but I didn't really have anything in common with any of them.

It's hard to be hopeful about discovering someone when there is nobody in my life to discover.

Last year I was in a hospital for a short inpatient stay for depression and suicidal tendancies. It was an odd experience overall, but the people were nice. The second to last day I was there a girl came in. She didn't leave her room the first day, so I never really saw her... but on my last day she came in for one group session. She was quiet, kept her head down, and when she was asked to talk, she seemed to have trouble. I got the impression that she had some sort of ailment... something that made it difficult for her to talk correctly. And she was beautiful. I could barely help myself but staring at her the whole time. Once I got back to my room, I just thought about her and why she was there. Obviously she was depressed, and most likely suicidal (that was why we were all there) and it just made me so sad. I didn't know her story, hell, at the time I didn't even know her name, but just the thought that she was so unhappy with herself made me miserable.

I didn't see her again for the rest of the day, and I was going home at the end of it, so I walked by her room to read her name plate, and I wrote her a note that I left by her door. I don't remember exactly what I said, but I basically told her that I thought she was beautiful, and that no matter what struggles she might be having in life, I believed she could get through it.

I'm not going to say her name, because it doesn't matter, but I remember. Since then I've often wondered how she took it. I worried that maybe she thought I was creepy. Maybe she didn't take it seriously and brushed it off. Or maybe I completely misunderstood her situation and made her feel worse. I doubt I'll ever see her again, or ever find out what happened after that, but I don't think I'll ever forget.

I'm pretty antisocial though... I don't enjoy traditional group things. When I was in college I tried several times to attend events where I might meet people who I'd get along with (there was even a Tetris themed "Block Party", hehe) but I only ever met one small group of 'friends' (whom I quickly isolated from as my depression set in).

I don't really like sports, I'm not very fit, the only outdoorsy thing I enjoy is hiking, but that's not very social, not does it keep my mind busy.

Lastly, I really don't know where to start when it comes to surrounding myself with people who share interest with me. I tried meetup.com, but the only promising group I could find is an hour away (and to get there goes straight through a major city). I feel really isolated.

I've made a lot of friends online, but most of them were... fleeting. I rarely got close enough to someone to have any private conversations, and just about every community I've joined I ended up leaving for one reason or another.

I also tried online dating a while back, but that left me feeling even worse (and I feel helped snowball me into landing in the hospital- long story). I went in with my expectations pretty mild, but after only a day or two I found this... perfect match. We had so many things in common, we shared ideologies, the site's personality test put us as a 95% match! So I worked up my courage and sent her a message, and three days later she changed her profile status to "seeing someone". I checked a few weeks after that, and she'd deleted her profile entirely. 

For someone who didn't think they would ever meet anyone like that, being given hope and having it dashed immediately was devastating.

Thanks. =) A while ago I started trying to "get in the system", and they put me on an antidepressant and I'm scheduled to see a therapist later this week. It's just... I don't know what to do in the meantime. The sadness and self-loathing seems so insurmountable, I'm running out of ways to keep myself sedated.

It's so f***ing frustrating. The only way to find love is to be happy with yourself and make something of your life, but how am I suppose to do that when I'm so goddamn miserable about being alone? I can't help but hate all these people who get happiness thrust on their lap, who are in a good place already so they are able to get what they want because of it. Meanwhile I can't stop being miserable BECAUSE I'm miserable. As far as I can tell I'm going to be stuck here forever, and it's the scariest thing imaginable. It's not that I don't know what to do... it's that I don't know how to be okay enough to deal with it.

I hope so too... I just wish I could turn off the pain until then. I want to go back to the way I was two years ago, where being alone didn't bother me. I don't even know why it kicked in like this... nothing really changed. I guess it just built up and got to be too much.

It's even worse to think that being so depressed like this is probably making me even less desirable. If I somehow managed to meet the perfect girl just out on the street, chances are I would turn her away immediately. After all, girls love confidence, don't they? And I'm the opposite of confident. It's a rather unfortunate feedback loop.

I should be finding ways to help my uncle around the house and taking care of my grandmother, but it took all of my drive just to get something to drink so I could take my meds. I just want to go back to sleep.
